Chapter 11
Product Sourcing
In this chapter, we delve into SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for
Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA, a dedicated
solution tailored to the unique needs of the automotive and industrial
manufacturing industries. We explore how this specialized software
seamlessly integrates with SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud
edition and SAP Business Network, offering a comprehensive ecosystem
that optimizes supplier management and drives collaboration within
the direct sourcing processes.
The unique sourcing requirements of the automotive and industrial manufacturing
sectors stem from the complex, highly engineered nature of their products, stringent
quality standards, and the need for resilience in the face of supply chain challenges.
Effective sourcing strategies in these industries require a deep understanding of tech-
nical specifications, global supplier networks, and a focus on quality, cost, and long-
term sustainability.
Traditional sourcing solutions often need more specialized capabilities to manage the
intricate bills of materials and stringent quality standards inherent to highly engi-
neered automotive and industrial manufacturing products. These solutions may strug-
gle to navigate the complexities of global supplier networks and regulatory compliance
specific to these industries. Consequently, the limitations of traditional sourcing tools
hinder procurement teams from effectively addressing the unique challenges and
requirements of materials cost management for such products, potentially leading to
quality issues, production delays, and increased costs.
SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in
SAP S/4HANA caters to the needs of automotive and industrial manufacturing indus-
tries. These solutions aim to assist procurement teams in streamlining sourcing proce-
dures for direct materials and cost optimization of complex, highly engineered
products. The solutions also offer benefits such as demand aggregation, supplier col-
laboration, and simplified operationalization of contract terms. This chapter of the
book provides a comprehensive overview of the suite, covering all its key components,
process areas, and configuration options, making it a valuable resource for anyone
seeking to leverage these solutions.

11.1 What Is Product Sourcing?
In the past, the automotive industry faced significant challenges with demand-driven
lifecycles, particularly during the product design phase for traditional gasoline-powered
cars. Lengthy lead times for design and manufacturing made it difficult to respond
swiftly to changing market conditions or consumer preferences. The industry’s inflex-
ible production lines and reliance on specific vehicle models hindered adaptability to
shifts in demand, leading to large inventories and increased costs.
Moreover, the risk of obsolescence loomed as consumer preferences shifted toward
electric vehicles (EVs) due to environmental concerns. Automotive companies, facing
pressure from stricter emissions regulations and market competition from innovative
EV startups, needed to make a fundamental shift in design and manufacturing pro-
cesses. As a result, many companies began investing heavily in EV technology, necessi-
tating not only a redesign of their products but also a transformation of their supply
chains and manufacturing methods to stay relevant in an era of electric mobility. This
transformation underscored the importance of adaptability in an industry undergoing
a profound shift toward sustainable transportation solutions.
The transformations in the supply chain have a profound impact on procurement pro-
cesses for several reasons. First, the emergence of global supply chains has expanded
the pool of potential suppliers, increasing the complexity of supplier selection and
evaluation. Second, advances in technology, such as supply chain automation and real-
time data analytics, enable more efficient and data-driven procurement decisions.
Third, the shift toward sustainable and responsible sourcing practices necessitates rig-
orous monitoring and compliance checks. Finally, the growing emphasis on supply
chain resilience, in the face of disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, compels pro-
curement teams to reassess risk management strategies and supplier relationships,
ultimately shaping the way they source goods and services.
A similar situation exists in the industrial manufacturing and components (IM&C)
industry. The heightened competition in this industry necessitates aggressive cost
management and rapid responses to market dynamics. With a more competitive land-
scape, companies must focus on cost efficiency to maintain profitability and remain
competitive. Quick responses to market changes, such as shifts in customer demand or
emerging trends, are vital for staying ahead of rivals and capturing new opportunities.
Moreover, fluctuations in commodity prices can significantly impact production costs.
Being able to swiftly adapt to these price changes, whether for raw materials or compo-
nents, is crucial to maintain pricing competitiveness and profit margins. Failing to
respond promptly to rising commodity costs, for example, can erode profitability or
result in higher product prices, potentially driving customers to competitors.
The role of procurement in IM&C is pivotal as it directly influences product quality,
cost, and supply chain efficiency. Procurement teams are responsible for sourcing raw
materials, components, and services, ensuring the timely delivery of materials to

support production. With innovations and process transformations, this role is grow-
ing in significance.
First, technological advancements in procurement, such as digital procurement plat-
forms and data analytics, empower teams to make informed decisions, optimize sup-
plier relationships, and identify cost-saving opportunities. Second, as these industries
evolve with innovations like EVs and Industry 4.0, procurement becomes essential for
securing specialized components and technologies. Third, sustainability and responsi-
ble sourcing are gaining prominence, making procurement instrumental in meeting
environmental and ethical standards in the supply chain. Finally, global supply chain
complexities require procurement professionals to navigate international markets,
logistics, and regulatory requirements, further emphasizing their role in driving oper-
ational excellence and maintaining a competitive edge in these dynamic industries.
As businesses transform their processes, they need modern ERP systems that can han-
dle large amounts of data, optimize workflows, and incorporate machine learning and
artificial intelligence. SAP is a popular choice for clients looking to upgrade their sys-
tems. However, with the end of support for SAP SRM, businesses are searching for pro-
curement solutions that align with their strategic vision.
SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in
SAP S/4HANA (see Figure 11.1) is an excellent option for sourcing and commodity man-
agement teams. It allows them to establish high-value agreements for direct materials,
such as raw materials, components, and assemblies. This solution is particularly useful
for industries with rapidly changing demand, as it improves supplier collaboration on
product development, shortening time to volume and reducing direct materials sourc-
ing costs. Moreover, because SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and
Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA is integrated with SAP S/4HANA, it supports
comprehensive sourcing program management and native access to procurement
execution systems, material masters, and contract management functionality.
As shown in Figure 11.1, the processes for development of new products (forward sourc-
ing) and product lifecycles encompass various stages from the initial design to the
eventual manufacturing and possible contract renegotiation. Here’s an overview of
each step:
1. Design product
The process begins with the design of a new product. During this stage, product spec-
ifications, features, and requirements are defined. Procurement teams collaborate
closely with design and engineering departments to ensure that the product’s
design is feasible and aligns with cost and sourcing considerations.
2. Develop procurement launch plan
After finalizing the product design, a procurement launch plan is developed. This
plan outlines the procurement strategy, supplier selection criteria, and sourcing
requirements. It also includes timelines and key milestones for sourcing the neces-
sary materials and components.

3. Source supply
With the procurement launch plan in place, the next step is to identify and source
the required materials, components, and suppliers. This involves supplier scouting,
negotiations, and contract agreements to secure a reliable supply chain for the pro-
duction of the new product.
4. Contract
Procurement teams establish contractual agreements with selected suppliers. Con-
tracts detail the terms and conditions of the supply, including pricing, delivery
schedules, quality standards, and any other relevant terms. Contracts are legally
binding and set the framework for the supplier-buyer relationship.
5. Procure supply
Once contracts are in place, the procurement team executes the procurement pro-
cess. This includes issuing purchase orders, managing supplier relationships, and
ensuring that the supply of materials and components is in alignment with the pro-
duction schedule.

6. Manufacture
The sourced materials and components are integrated into the manufacturing pro-
cess. The production of the new product begins, and quality control measures are
implemented to ensure that the final product meets design specifications and cus-
tomer expectations.
7. Renegotiate contracts
Over time, as the product progresses through its lifecycle, it may become necessary
to revisit supplier contracts. This can involve renegotiating terms, adjusting pricing,
or accommodating changes in product design. The aim is to ensure that the supply
chain remains efficient, cost-effective, and responsive to market demands.
In the upcoming sections, we will explore each component of the integrated suite of
product sourcing solutions from SAP (see Figure 11.2), providing a comprehensive
understanding of how these tools can enhance procurement and sourcing processes in
various industries. This deeper dive will highlight the specific features and benefits of
each component, offering insights into their practical applications and value for busi-
nesses.

SAP S/4HANA for supplier quotation management, as detailed in Section 11.6, serves as
a catalyst for enhanced collaboration between manufacturers and suppliers. This tech-
nology allows suppliers to bid on product development competitively, fostering a cul-
ture of supplier-driven innovation. In turn, manufacturers use it to elevate the
customer experience, curtail direct materials sourcing costs, and expedite time-to-
market.
Furthermore, SAP’s product sourcing solutions seamlessly integrate with SAP S/4HANA
and SAP Business Technology Platform, granting them direct access to material mas-
ters. This integration streamlines the creation of operational documents such as con-
tracts and purchase orders, aligning them effortlessly with sourcing terms and
conditions. This enhanced source-to-contract process not only simplifies operations
but also enhances transparency.
In the upcoming sections, we’ll delve into three essential subprojects within the pro-
curement process. First, we’ll explore the intricacies of the sourcing project, where you
can initiate supplier engagement and gather proposals. Following that, we’ll delve into
the critical quotation evaluation phase, where you can assess supplier submissions to
make informed decisions. Finally, we’ll discuss the vital step of transmitting awarded
information to a central purchasing contracts system, ensuring seamless integration
between the sourcing efforts and contract management processes. These subprojects
collectively contribute to the efficiency and effectiveness of procurement operations.
11.2.1 Sourcing Project
The request for quotation (RFQ) process in materials management plays a vital role in
procurement but has its limitations. It can be time-consuming due to manual steps
involved, particularly when dealing with numerous vendors.
It is worth noting that this document still requires completely manual intervention.
For certain industries, this becomes critical due to the large number of suppliers, posi-
tions, conditions, and the inability to compare large supplier quotations.
Users can actively monitor their existing list of sourcing projects (see Figure 11.3). It’s
essential to do so to stay informed about the current statuses, number of participants,
and other information for each project. This monitoring ensures that procurement
teams can proactively manage and optimize their sourcing efforts, make informed
decisions, and address any issues or delays promptly.
If you’re looking for a comprehensive solution for sourcing projects, SAP S/4HANA
offers a powerful tool. This sourcing project tool offers similar functions to RFQ (see
Figure 11.4), but with added features such as complex item and milestone management,
demand planning, and access to supplier lists.

11.2.2 Quotation Evaluation
Once suppliers submit their quotations via SAP S/4HANA for supplier quotation man-
agement, they become accessible for evaluation and comparison within the sourcing
project. The Supplier Quotations tab, as shown in Figure 11.10, displays up-to-date infor-
mation about supplier responses. Users can efficiently compare multiple quotations,
assess attachments and supporting documents, and monitor quotation statuses. This
tab streamlines communication with suppliers, facilitates in-depth analysis, and
empowers procurement professionals to make informed decisions that align with their
organization’s strategic goals.
A supplier quotation submitted in a sourcing project typically includes detailed infor-
mation such as the supplier’s proposed prices and clear breakdown of pricing, includ-
ing potential cost-saving discounts and payment terms. It also outlines delivery
information and payment terms. In addition, suppliers may include any relevant
terms and conditions and attachments required to meet the sourcing project’s specifi-
cations.
Figure 11.10 Sourcing Project: Supplier Quotations
As a useful tool in the sourcing process, the sourcing manager can review supplier quo-
tations and easily compare them by clicking the Compare Quotations button. This
allows for a fair and thorough evaluation of each proposal, with the top contenders
moving forward to the negotiation stage. The Compare Supplier Quotations app dis-
plays an overview of all quotations for a sourcing project.
Within the Compare Supplier Quotations app, as shown in Figure 11.11, you can stream-
line the process of analysis and comparison in several ways:

11 Product Sourcing
430
 Pin and compare
You have the option to pin up to two quotations, enabling a side-by-side comparison
against all other received quotations. This feature provides a convenient way to focus
on specific supplier responses while considering the broader pool of quotations.
 Total cost calculation
The application facilitates the calculation of the total cost, taking into account all rel-
evant factors, such as unit prices, quantities, and any associated discounts or sur-
charges. This allows for a comprehensive assessment of the overall cost implications
for each supplier.
 Price breakdown
You can delve into the price breakdown for each quotation, which provides a
detailed analysis of how the total cost is distributed among various cost compo-
nents. This breakdown helps in identifying areas of cost variance and understanding
the drivers behind each supplier's pricing.
 Create awarding scenarios
The Compare Supplier Quotations app empowers you to create awarding scenarios
tailored to your sourcing and procurement objectives.
 Initiate negotiations
If negotiations are required, the application allows you to initiate communication
with suppliers directly from the platform. This functionality streamlines the negoti-
ation process by providing a centralized platform for discussions, clarifications, and
potential revisions to the quotations.

11.2 Product Sourcing
In the negotiation process within the sourcing project, as shown in Figure 11.12, the
sourcing manager plays a pivotal role by selecting several supplier quotations and ini-
tiating negotiations to optimize material sourcing outcomes. This process allows for
the exploration of various negotiation strategies to secure the best possible terms. Fur-
thermore, you can find a similar negotiation process in the guided sourcing capability
for SAP Ariba Sourcing, making it a best practice.
This solution enables the selection of multiple items within supplier quotations for
doing mass changes. For instance, a sourcing manager can swiftly reduce the target
price by 15 percent across several items from one or multiple supplier quotations,
enhancing efficiency in negotiation adjustments.
In addition, the negotiation process is tracked with specific status assignments, provid-
ing visibility into the negotiation’s lifecycle stage. In other words, this feature helps
sourcing managers monitor the progress and status of negotiations, ensuring align-
ment with category sourcing strategies and procurement goals. Like in guided sourcing
capability for SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive
and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA excels in facilitating these negotiation
practices, enhancing procurement effectiveness and aligning with strategic objectives.

11.3 Procurement Planning
As shown in Figure 11.1, the process of product design and procurement planning is
vital in any company. To ensure smooth operations, it is crucial to integrate procure-
ment systems with product lifecycle management (PLM) systems. SAP Ariba Direct
Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA
offers an excellent cloud-based version of SAP Ariba Procurement Planning. This solu-
tion provides various capabilities, including simplified importing of parts lists from
different PLM systems, automated backward scheduling of critical milestones before
product launch, and bundling of raw materials, parts, and assemblies across product
lines to maximize benefits during sourcing processes.
After the procurement launch plan is in place and necessary investments have been
agreed upon, SAP Ariba Procurement Planning seamlessly integrates with SAP Ariba
Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA
to kickstart sourcing projects and effectively manage ongoing milestones. This method
guarantees that the sourcing strategy is continuously updated, thereby streamlining the
sourcing process and enhancing productivity.
Figure 11.15 Procurement Project
In the procurement planning process, two key roles play a crucial part: the project man-
ager and the investment planner. They are responsible for managing procurement
projects with regard to the schedule and investment planning. With the help of the

11 Product Sourcing
434
Manage Procurement Projects app (see Figure 11.15), they can define projects, create
subprojects, and assign a bill of materials (BOM) that contains the items that need to be
planned.
The project manager or investment planner can plan procurement activities well in
advance, taking into consideration both the time schedule and investment planning of
items based on a central bill of materials. SAP Ariba Procurement Planning empowers
you to plan the sourcing of items from the early stages, ensuring timely procurement
before the manufacturing process begins.
In the following sections, we’ll explore three crucial aspects of procurement planning
in SAP S/4HANA. First, we’ll delve into identifying necessary items for subprojects
using the BOM. Then we’ll focus on creating reliable project timelines through mile-
stones and task scheduling methods. Finally, we’ll discover how bundling similar items
together enhances procurement efficiency. These topics are fundamental to effective
procurement planning within SAP S/4HANA, providing practical insights for successful
procurement projects.
11.3.1 Parts Import and Assignment to Projects
In the BOM section (see Figure 11.16), the project manager or investment planner has the
ability to identify the BOMs that include the necessary items for the subproject and are
essential for planning purposes. Users can create a customized filter for each BOM to
facilitate the initial import of items and for any manual BOM refreshes that you initiate.

To manually create items for the subproject, the project manager or investment plan-
ner has the option of choosing the Manually Create Items button in the BOM Assign-
ments section. Doing so will automatically include the created items in the subproject
item table, allowing users to conveniently manage them alongside other project items.
To ensure that subproject users have the most up-to-date information on assigned
items (see Figure 11.17), it’s recommended to trigger a BOM refresh. This will ensure that

Figure 11.17 Items of Procurement Project
11.3.2 Milestones and Task Scheduling
To calculate a schedule at an item level, users need to assign a BOM to the subproject in
the Manage Procurement Projects app. Once this is done, users can navigate to the sub-
project and its item detailed page (as shown in Figure 11.18) and then access the Sched-
ule section to trigger an item schedule calculation by selecting Calculate Schedule. The
system will then calculate the time schedule and generate a list of its corresponding
milestones, events, and tasks (including their dates) based on the assigned item sched-
uling template, which is automatically selected by the system.
It’s important to note that when calculating the schedule for the specification deadline
or supplier award deadline event, the system will only calculate the planned date. This
means that users can rely on the system to provide them with a reliable timeline for
their procurement projects but should also be aware that some manual adjustments
may be necessary based on factors such as unforeseen delays or changes in project
scope.

11.3.3 Parts Bundling per Sourcing Needs
For users with the purchaser bundling role, the Manage Bundles app (see Figure 11.19) is
a valuable tool that helps them group similar items together into bundles to achieve
higher volumes of sourcing. With this app, purchaser bundling can easily create
detailed bundles that can be passed on to the sourcing department. Once the bundles
are complete, they are ready to be handed over to start the sourcing process. This effi-
cient process can help streamline the sourcing workflow and increase productivity.
An efficient way to organize items based on sourcing requirements is by utilizing the
automatic bundling feature. The system performs this task by considering a specific
bundling criterion, which could be any item attribute such as node type, material num-
ber, or package. The automatic bundling process generates a preview of the bundles
and assigns all unassigned items to them. After that, users can review and modify each
bundle as needed before applying the preview changes. This feature helps streamline
the sourcing process and saves users time and effort.
When transferring a bundle to a sourcing application, the following objects are created
automatically in the sourcing application:
 Sourcing project
 Procurement project
 Project item
 Invest item

11.4 Product Sourcing with Enterprise Contract Management
By integrating SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Man-
ufacturing in SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management
with the ability to include Icertis part, you gain the advantage of being able to effort-
lessly create, update, and assign legal transactions and documents from either a sourc-
ing project or a supplier quotation.
SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management plays a pivotal role in sourcing proj-
ects by offering a comprehensive set of capabilities. Its primary purpose is to streamline
and optimize contract management throughout the entire sourcing project lifecycle.
First, SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management ensures contract standardiza-
tion by providing templates and predefined clauses, ensuring that contracts align with
legal and regulatory requirements, fostering consistency and compliance.
Second, it expedites the contract authoring process, allowing the sourcing manager to cre-
ate contracts swiftly and accurately using standardized templates. Moreover, SAP S/4HANA
for enterprise contract management automates contract-related workflows, including
approvals and notifications, reducing delays and manual intervention in sourcing projects.
This automation enhances visibility and control over contract progress.
Furthermore, SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management helps mitigate con-
tractual risks by facilitating compliance with legal standards, aligning contracts with
organizational policies, and reducing the likelihood of disputes.

11.5 Product Sourcing and Commodity Pricing Engine
After creating a legal transaction in sourcing projects, you can do the following:
 Create legal documents as attachments or virtual documents.
 Categorize legal documents as important so that they are displayed as such in the
sourcing projects.

11.5 Product Sourcing and Commodity Pricing Engine
In a sourcing project that involves multiple commodities, it’s essential to have detailed
information about each commodity’s quantity and cost. Once the procurement pro-
cess is completed, a central purchase contract can be generated based on the supplier’s
quotation. The commodities can be managed across sourcing projects, supplier quota-
tions, and central purchase contracts. For materials, you can even specify the update
cycle for each commodity, which determines the frequency of updating the commod-
ity’s price conditions in the central contract.
By integrating the optional commodity pricing engine within SAP S/4HANA for com-
modity management for physical contracts, real-time commodity pricing becomes
accessible through SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial
Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA. It’s worth noting that, as of now, this real-time pricing
functionality is exclusively available for on-premise or private cloud deployments.
This means that organizations using these deployment options can seamlessly access
and leverage up-to-the-minute commodity pricing data, enhancing their procurement
and sourcing activities with dynamic and current market insights. Commodity pricing
plays a pivotal role in enhancing procurement strategies and contract negotiations.
Leveraging this feature, organizations can access real-time commodity pricing data,
historical trends, and market intelligence to inform their decision-making. During sup-
plier negotiations, this data serves as an objective reference point, ensuring that pric-
ing discussions are grounded in current market conditions, leading to more equitable
and favorable agreements. Organizations can link contracts to specific commodity
price indices or utilize pricing benchmarks to determine contract terms, resulting in
contracts that are adaptable to market fluctuations.
The commodity pricing engine streamlines the process of calculating prices for com-
modities or products containing commodities traded at exchanges by integrating with
external data sources, applying pricing algorithms, and supporting index-based pric-
ing.

440
11.6 Quotation Management and Supplier Quotations
During the era of online collaboration with suppliers, essential business processes
migrated to digital platforms. Since the era of SAP SRM, companies have begun to
understand that interaction with suppliers online brings significant benefits and dra-
matically changes the company’s procurement processes. This transformation
occurred to bolster efficiency, streamline communication, and ensure real-time access
to critical data, enabling companies to respond rapidly to market changes and enhance
